Stability of ratings between rounds

Source: R/stability.R
delphi_stability.Rd

Measures, for every item and indicator, how much the ratings change between consecutive rounds, and tests whether they are stable. Two stability criteria are available:

  • Wilcoxon (default): a Wilcoxon test comparing the two rounds. With linked experts it is the paired signed-rank test on the experts who answered both rounds; otherwise it is the rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test on the two independent samples. The item is stable when the test is not significant (p_value >= alpha).

  • Net change between distributions: a criterion based on Scheibe, Skutsch and Schofer (1975). The item is stable when the net change between the two rating distributions, computed as described in Details, is at most scheibe (15% by default).

Usage

delphi_stability(
  x,
  method = c("wilcoxon", "scheibe", "both"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  scheibe = 0.15,
  rounds = NULL,
  indicator = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  bins = 10,
  type = 7,
  exact = FALSE,
  paired = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object with at least two rounds.

method

Stability criterion used for the stable column: "wilcoxon", "scheibe" or "both" (stable only if both criteria agree). Both criteria are always reported.

alpha

Significance level of the Wilcoxon test. Default 0.05.

scheibe

Largest share of net change that still counts as stable under the net-change criterion. Default 0.15.

rounds

Optional round numbers to compare. Consecutive rounds among them are compared (for example c(1, 3) compares round 1 with round 3). NULL compares all consecutive rounds.

indicator, items

Optional subsets of indicators and items.

bins

Number of classes used to build the rating distributions for the net-change criterion on long scales. Scales with up to bins points use one class per scale point; longer scales are split into bins equal classes (for example 1 to 10, 11 to 20, ..., 91 to 100). Default 10.

type

Quantile algorithm for medians and IQRs; see delphi_describe().

exact

Passed to stats::wilcox.test(). The default FALSE uses the normal approximation with continuity correction, which handles the ties and zero differences that are common with rating scales.

paired

Whether to compare the rounds expert by expert. By default (NULL) the comparison is paired when the experts are linked across rounds (linked = TRUE in delphi_data()) and unpaired otherwise. paired = TRUE is not allowed for unlinked experts.

Value

A data frame of class delphi_stability with one row per indicator, item and pair of rounds, and columns indicator, item, round_from, round_to, n_from, n_to, n_paired, median_from, median_to, median_change, iqr_from, iqr_to, iqr_change, changed, p_value, scheibe_change, stable_wilcoxon, stable_scheibe and stable. The settings are stored in the "rule" attribute.

Details

Medians and IQRs are always computed on all experts who answered each round (n_from, n_to), as in delphi_describe().

The ratings of each round are grouped into classes (one class per scale point, or bins classes on long scales), and the net change is $$C = \frac{1}{2} \sum_k \left| p_k^{(t)} - p_k^{(t-1)} \right|,$$ where \(p_k^{(t)}\) is the share of experts in class \(k\) in round \(t\). \(C\) is the share of experts who would have to move to another class to turn one distribution into the other.

In the paired comparison, the test, the share of experts who changed their rating (changed) and the net change are computed on the experts who answered the item in both rounds (n_paired), so that drop-outs are not mistaken for changes of opinion.

In the unpaired comparison, used when the same expert cannot be identified in both rounds, the test is the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and the net change is computed on all the experts who answered each round; n_paired and changed are NA. Since the two samples may include different experts, a difference between rounds reflects both changes of opinion and changes in the composition of the panel.

When the two rounds contain exactly the same ratings, the item is stable under both criteria (p_value = 1, net change 0).

References

Scheibe, M., Skutsch, M. and Schofer, J. (1975). Experiments in Delphi methodology. In H. A. Linstone and M. Turoff (Eds.), The Delphi Method: Techniques and Applications (pp. 262-287). Reading, MA: Addison-Wesley.

See also

delphi_status() to combine stability with consensus.

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
delphi_stability(x)
#> Stability criterion: Wilcoxon signed-rank test, stable if p >= 0.05
#> Paired comparison on the experts who answered both rounds.
#> 
#>     indicator item round_from round_to n_paired median_from median_to iqr_from
#>        impact   E1          1        2       13           7         8     1.50

#>        impact   E6          1        2       12           3         3     3.75
#>        impact   E7          1        2       13           8         8     2.50
#>        impact   E8          1        2       12           4         5     3.00
#>  plausibility   E1          1        2       13          77        78    18.50
#>  plausibility   E2          1        2       12          28        30    21.75
#>  plausibility   E3          1        2       13          62        60    19.00

# Net-change criterion only, on the impact ratings
delphi_stability(x, method = "scheibe", indicator = "impact")
